documentation.title: Network & Recovery
documentation.body:
The Heltec WiFi LoRa 32 V3 is a **WiFi-only** board — no ethernet PHY. ESPHome's transport selector in MajiFlow is locked on WiFi.

| Property | Value |
|---|---|
| Default for this board | WiFi (forced) |
| Credentials needed | SSID + password |
| Diagnostic sensors | `wifi_info` (IP, SSID, MAC) + `wifi_signal` (dBm) |
| Static IP support | ✓ via *Connection → IP Configuration* |
| Recovery if wifi goes down | Improv or join the fallback AP (see below) |

### Where the dashboard lives

The entity dashboard only serves on the device's **wifi-station** IP — the IP your router assigns it, or whatever you set as `manual_ip`. It does **not** serve at `192.168.4.1` (the fallback-AP gateway). ESPHome's `web_server` doesn't bind the SoftAP interface ([esphome/issues#4333](https://github.com/esphome/issues/issues/4333)), so when wifi is down there is no entity-control surface.

To control the device, it must be on a wifi network the laptop can also reach.

### Recovery

When wifi credentials need changing, use one of these. Neither restores the dashboard until wifi rejoins.

**1. Improv Wi-Fi** — recommended. Open standard from the Home Assistant ecosystem (github.com/improv-wifi). Two flavours, both compiled in:

- **BLE** (`esp32_improv`): pair from any Chromium-based browser at [improv-wifi.com](https://www.improv-wifi.com/). WebBluetooth talks **directly** to the device — no server, no account.
- **Serial** (`improv_serial`): same page, but over USB via WebSerial.

**2. Fallback AP + captive portal** — works without a Chromium browser.

- After ~90 s of failed wifi association, the device broadcasts `<friendly_name> Fallback` (password = your wifi password).
- Joining the AP triggers the OS captive-portal popup automatically.
- Use that popup's **Configure WiFi** form to enter new credentials.
- On ESPHome 2025.2.0+ the popup may render blank — the credential-save endpoint still works behind the scenes, but if so prefer Improv.
- Typing `http://192.168.4.1/` directly shows nothing useful; don't bother.

### Web dashboard

Emitted on **port 80**, reachable at the device's wifi IP. Every relay, sensor, switch, and number entity declared in the topology is exposed for manual control.

### Range note

The Heltec's WiFi antenna is the chip antenna on the board edge. For installations behind metal enclosures or far from the access point, plan a WiFi repeater or use the LoRa transport instead (entity-level — not the ESPHome network transport).

documentation.title: Power Requirements
documentation.body:
The Heltec V3 is a low-power node. It can run from USB-C, 3.7 V Li-Po (battery JST connector), or external 5 V on the Vin pin.

| Source | Notes |
|---|---|
| USB-C | 5 V — recommended for desk/dev work and as a charger when a battery is plugged in |
| Li-Po (JST 1.25 mm, MX1.25) | 3.7 V nominal, 4.2 V full. The onboard charger handles charging when USB-C is also plugged in |
| Vin pin | 5 V regulated; do not exceed 5.5 V |

**Idle current** (WiFi connected, OLED off): ~80 mA at 5 V. **OLED on**: +20 mA. **Transmit burst** (WiFi or LoRa): up to 250 mA peak — keep the supply ≥ 500 mA capable.

**Battery longevity**: deep-sleep with WiFi off + LoRa periodic wake yields months on a 2000 mAh Li-Po. WiFi station mode awake 24/7 is closer to 24 hours per 1000 mAh.

**Vext**: GPIO36 controls a 3.3 V output rail (`vext`) that powers the OLED + sensor headers. The board package auto-toggles it when sampling sensors — if you wire external 3.3 V devices off Vext, they will brown-out during sleep.

documentation.title: On-Board Peripherals
documentation.body:
### OLED display

128×64 SSD1306 over I²C. Wired to **SDA: GPIO17, SCL: GPIO18, RESET: GPIO21**, address `0x3C`. ESPHome's display component renders text + graphics. The board package emits a default splash and renders status fields whenever the topology declares an OLED-bearing system.

**Power**: the OLED is on the Vext rail (GPIO36). On battery profiles, MajiFlow toggles Vext only during periodic refresh.

### LoRa radio (SX1262)

The SX1262 chip on the board is wired over SPI:

| Function | GPIO |
|---|---|
| SCK | GPIO9 |
| MOSI | GPIO10 |
| MISO | GPIO11 |
| NSS (CS) | GPIO8 |
| BUSY | GPIO13 |
| DIO1 | GPIO14 |
| RESET | GPIO12 |

These pins are reserved by the board package — do not assign topology entities to them. Use the LoRa transport at the **entity** level (e.g. cross-system links over LoRa) — this is independent of the ESPHome `wifi:` / `ethernet:` transport for HA connectivity.

**Antenna**: the board ships with a 868/915 MHz spring antenna. For range > 50 m through walls, swap to a 1/4-wave whip on the IPEX (U.FL) connector.

### Battery monitoring

A divider on **GPIO1** (ADC1_CH0) reads the Li-Po voltage. The board package emits `sensor.battery_voltage` and a `sensor.battery_percent` derived via per-board calibration tables (linear interpolation between voltage→percent datapoints in `peripherals.battery.calibration`).

### LED

A single white LED on **GPIO35**. Used by self-test for blink probe, but free for topology use (e.g. heartbeat indicator).
